The research ESCALATION fast-lane is still 100% broken. Scout/coverage-critic request a deep escalation via scripts/escalate-research.js -> `gh workflow run research-agent.yml -f tier=deep` using the job GITHUB_TOKEN (scout-agent.yml / coverage-critic-agent.yml set GH_TOKEN: github.token), so the dispatched run's actor is github-actions[bot]. anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 resolves to a newer action build that gates non-human actors and rejects bot actors unless listed in allowed_bots; no step in research-agent.yml sets it (default = allow no bots). Every escalated research run therefore dies at its claude-code-action step with 'Action failed with error: Workflow initiated by non-human actor: github-actions (type: Bot). OWNER FIX NEEDED (protected .github/workflows/research-agent.yml) — ALREADY TRACKED by OPEN issue #430: add `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` to the with: block of the two deep-tier claude-code-action@v1 steps (Fable 5 'deep, preferred' and Opus 4.8 'deep fallback'). Per the action source the matcher lowercases and strips a trailing [bot], so `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` correctly matches the github-actions[bot] actor. Scope to the trusted first-party Actions bot; do NOT use `*` on this public repo. CAVEAT (documented in #430): setting allowed_bots can move the token out of .git/config into a credential helper, so the deep steps' in-prompt `git push` may lose the checkout@v5-persisted credentials unless `github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` is ALSO added to the two deep steps. Leave the standard scheduled step untouched (it works today).

Could NOT author the fix: this is the unattended Self-repair CI agent (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true/CI=true), so the CI-only scripts/hooks/protect-automation.js PreToolUse hook fires and BLOCKS any Edit/Write/Bash mutation of .github/workflows/** ('A human must author changes to these files'). Re-confirmed this run: on a self-repair/ branch the Edit adding allowed_bots to research-agent.yml was blocked by the hook (exit 2); branch abandoned, working tree clean. By design an unattended CI agent cannot author protected-path (.github/workflows/**) changes — the hook is a hard safety invariant and was NOT circumvented (no env-var/API/indirect-write workaround attempted) — so no PR is possible and the fix must be applied by a human.

No non-protected fix exists: the breakage is the bot-actor gate on the dispatched run. Any GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated `gh workflow run`/repository_dispatch produces a Bot actor regardless of event, so changing escalate-research.js cannot make the dispatch a human actor without a new PAT secret + workflow wiring (itself a protected change). The allowed_bots (+github_token) addition to the two deep steps is the correct, minimal fix.
